title: CAPTOR: a vision-language foundation model for Chest-Abdomen-Pelvis Oncologic CT
abstract: arXiv:2610.14226v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Purpose : To develop and evaluate CAPTOR, a deep-learning vision-language foundation model for oncologic chest-abdomen-pelvis (CAP) CT interpretation.   Materials & Methods : CAPTOR (Chest-Abdomen-Pelvis foundaTion model for Oncologic Radiology) is a contrastive vision-language model, trained using a pretraining strategy for oncologic CAP CT (in single- or multiple-series acquisitions), on a multicenter retrospective dataset from North America, Europe and Asia, predominantly from tumor lesion examinations. CAPTOR was compared with state-of-the-art CT foundation models on three downstream tasks: disease detection, survival prediction using TumorImagingBench and image retrieval. Classification and retrieval were both evaluated on held-out internal and public test sets, stratified by anatomical coverage and indication. Bootstrap resampling was used to estimate confidence intervals, and pairwise comparisons were performed using permutation

translated_title: CAPTOR：用于胸腹盆肿瘤CT的视觉-语言基础模型
translated_abstract: 目的：开发并评估CAPTOR，一个用于胸腹盆（CAP）CT肿瘤学解读的深度学习视觉-语言基础模型。材料与方法：CAPTOR（胸腹盆肿瘤放射学基础模型）是一种对比式视觉-语言模型，采用针对肿瘤学CAP CT（单序列或多序列采集）的预训练策略，在来自北美、欧洲和亚洲的多中心回顾性数据集上进行训练，该数据集主要来源于肿瘤病灶检查。CAPTOR在三个下游任务上与最先进的CT基础模型进行了比较：疾病检测、使用TumorImagingBench进行的生存预测以及图像检索。分类和检索均在留出的内部和公开测试集上进行评估，并按解剖覆盖范围和适应症进行分层。使用Bootstrap重采样估计置信区间，并采用置换检验进行成对比较。
tldr: 该论文提出了CAPTOR，一个基于多中心肿瘤数据预训练的胸腹盆CT视觉-语言基础模型，在疾病检测、生存预测和图像检索三项下游任务上优于现有最先进的CT基础模型。
en_tdlr: CAPTOR is a contrastive vision-language foundation model pretrained on multicenter oncologic chest-abdomen-pelvis CT data, outperforming state-of-the-art CT foundation models on disease detection, survival prediction, and image retrieval tasks.
